name: Harry Huynh
title: Information Technology Engineer
currentFocus: Endpoint reliability, practical automation, backup readiness, and clear technical documentation

hero.headline: I build dependable IT systems and keep the useful details written down.
hero.summary: I am Harry Huynh, an Information Technology Engineer focused on practical infrastructure, troubleshooting, documentation, and the calm operational habits that help people work without technical friction.

biography: My work sits close to the everyday places where technology either helps or gets in the way: laptops, networks, identity, backup routines, cloud tools, and the small operational decisions that make a team feel supported.
I like systems that are understandable. A good fix should not only solve today's issue; it should leave behind notes, checks, and handoff details that make tomorrow easier.
Outside the technical work, this site is also a personal archive for writing and photography. The goal is to show the person behind the engineering without turning the portfolio into a sales page.
principles: Make the system easy to understand before making it clever.
Document the decision, not just the command that happened to work.
Prefer boring reliability for anything people depend on daily.
Keep personal work honest: real projects, real photos, real notes.

experience.summary: Hands-on infrastructure and support work across endpoint setup, network hygiene, backup planning, automation, and technical documentation.
achievements: Built repeatable setup notes for common workstation and account onboarding tasks.
Organized backup and recovery checks into lightweight routines that can be reviewed without a dedicated admin panel.
Created this website as a static, Git-backed personal archive for work, writing, and photography.

experience.summary: A practical lab for testing deployment flows, local hosting, networking notes, and small automations before using them in public-facing work.
achievements: Uses the Git repository as the source of truth for publishing content.
Keeps hosting simple enough to run from this computer or export to static hosting later.
Treats documentation as part of the finished project, not an afterthought.
